name: git-sync
description: Sync PersonalClaw state between your machines through a git remote you own. The transport keeps a local working clone and moves durability shard objects as files it commits and pushes, so `git log -p` over the shards is a human-diffable audit history of what the assistant knows — the whole point of this transport. It stays plaintext (never encrypted) so that history stays readable; secrets are excluded upstream and never touch it.
author: PersonalClaw

x-meta.label: Git remote URL
x-meta.help: The ssh or https URL of a git remote you own (both machines point at the same one). A remote at a local path is refused, and so is an https URL with a user name or token written into it (put the token in Access token), or an ssh one with a password (ssh signs in with your key). Leave empty to configure later — the transport stays idle until set.

x-meta.label: Local working clone
x-meta.help: Where the working clone lives on this machine. Supports ~ and $VARS. The transport clones the remote here on first use and reuses it after.

x-meta.label: Branch
x-meta.help: The branch to sync on. Both machines must use the same branch.

x-meta.label: Access token
x-meta.help: For an https remote that needs a token to sign in: an access token from your git host. It is kept in PersonalClaw's credential store and handed to git by its own credential helper, never written into the working clone or onto a command line. Only an https remote is given it (or an http one on this machine). Leave empty for ssh, which signs in with your ssh key.

x-meta.label: User name
x-meta.help: The user name to sign in with alongside Access token, if your host wants one. Leave empty to sign in as x-access-token, which a host that checks only the token accepts; set your account's name for a host that wants it with its token. Leave empty for ssh.
